hints: Look carefully at what is on each axis, rate of reaction against time, and ask yourself when substrate concentration is highest in this closed tube.
Remember that rate depends on successful enzyme-substrate collisions, so think about what happens to collision frequency and rate as that fixed amount of substrate is gradually used up to zero.
walkthrough:
**Picture the start of the reaction**

At time 0 you have just mixed a fixed amount of enzyme and substrate. Substrate concentration is at its maximum.

That means the chance of enzyme-substrate collisions is highest, so the rate of reaction starts at its maximum value, not at zero.

**Follow what happens as time passes**

As the reaction proceeds, substrate is converted to product and is not replaced. Substrate concentration steadily falls.

Fewer substrate molecules means fewer enzyme-substrate complexes per second, so the rate steadily decreases.

**Finish when the reaction is complete**

The question says the reaction is left until it is complete. That means all substrate is eventually used up.

With $[substrate] = 0$, no more reaction can occur, so rate $= 0$. A curve that starts high and falls smoothly to zero matches graph C.

options.A: Shows rate increasing steadily with time. This is backwards, as substrate is being used up, not added, so rate cannot keep rising.
options.B: Shows rate starting at zero then levelling at a high steady value. This confuses rate with total product, product levels off but rate must fall to zero.
options.C: Shows rate highest at the start then falling to zero. This is correct because substrate is maximal at first and then depleted until the reaction stops.
options.D: Shows rate starting at zero, rising to a peak, then falling. Rate cannot start at zero here because plenty of substrate is present at time 0.
